analysis.title: GS Blekos - Marketcolour 19 Oct 2026
key_insights: US equities fell Friday amid continued pressure in the AI/debt/funding trade: SPX -109bps to 7659, NDX -250bps to 29,187 (below 50/100 dma, -550bps on the week), RTY -166bps to 2721. VIX +20% to 19.98. Futures traded 3.6x the 20-day average.

Info Tech fell 254bps and Comm. Services fell 245bps. SOX fell 3.4% and semis have an 8-day losing streak. Global Neoclouds (GSXGNEOC) fell 902bps, extending recent losses. Energy rose 246bps, with Nat Gas stocks (GSENNATG) up 395bps, a 2.8 sigma move.

European equities closed the week firm (SXXP +70bps, SX5E +60bps), the index's strongest weekly gain since July. The advance was broad, led by Defense (GSSBDEFE +4%), Renewables (GSXERNEW +1.7%) and Autos (GSXEAUTO +1.7%).
14% of the SPX reports earnings this week. GS says the next move depends on earnings confirmation.

Fundamental LS hedge funds lost 2.7% last week (alpha -1.1%), their worst week since July, but are still up 9.8% YTD. The global book saw its largest weekly net selling since end of July, with all regions net sold, led by EM. Info Tech was the most net sold sector and saw the largest net selling on GS records. Health Care and Comm. Services were the most net bought.

US L/S gross leverage rose 0.9 pts to 213.9% (56th percentile one-year). US L/S net leverage fell 3.2 pts to 43.7% (0th percentile five-year). That is the largest weekly decline since April 2025 and the 4th largest in five years.
Nearly $10bn flowed into levered ETFs last week, the largest weekly inflow in GS's dataset. SOXL (3x semis) took a record +$7bn, 74% of net inflows. TQQQ (3x NDX) added +$1.3bn.

US Strategy recommends consumer-facing laggards for a catch-up (low-income consumer discretionary, GSXULOWD). It also highlights a screen of 23 defensive Health Care and Staples stocks with quality attributes (Exhibit 19) for investors worried about further catch-down.

GS sentiment and positioning indicator fell to the 46th percentile, its lowest since April, decoupled from strong global PMIs. The largest drags were stronger fixed income fund flows, the Risk Appetite Indicator falling below zero, and increased positioning in Gold and JPY. Equity vol rose modestly, much less than bond vol. CTA and risk parity positioning remains risk-off.

DHL raised FY26 EBIT guidance to >€7.0bn from >€6.5bn, as expected (GSe €7.1bn, company consensus €6.9bn). Q3 EBIT was €1.71bn vs GSe €1.68bn and company consensus €1.65bn. Express EBIT was about €1bn, in line, with a c.€100mn benefit from air freight capacity constraints. FCF was €900mn, in line. FY FCF guide rose to €3.2bn from €3.0bn while capex guidance rose to €3.6bn from €3-3.3bn. Company sees a robust Q4 seasonal peak and will review mid-term EBIT guidance in March.

GIR reinstated coverage of European satellites: Buy on SES (€7.0 PT) and Neutral on Eutelsat (€1.6 PT). For SES, GIR sees an attractive entry after recent weakness, with upside from incoming C-band cash and higher space-defence spending. Upside is 79% to the base-case PT and >180% in a blue-sky scenario.

Reinsurer previews are negative: GS is 18% below consensus for SREN, 5% below for Scor, and its P&C Re COR for MUV2 is 2pp less favourable than consensus. The stocks have squeezed on the move to defensives, and SREN is back at peak multiple despite weaker P&L quality and top-line pressure.
